segments.text: By then, the war had changed again armies that had invaded one another's worlds now fought alongside their former enemies.
They had finally found something they feared more than one another.
We were caught between those armies as the crossings began to fail.
Roads vanished into smoke. Bridges collapsed. And the confusion, Kesh, broke.
And I were driven apart.
I remember running through ruins with my sketchbook pressed against my chest.
It was a foolish thing to carry through a battle.
Yet, I was more afraid of losing those drawings than I was willing to admit.
For a long time, I didn't know whether my friends at Survive News came from places
I couldn't reach.
Through soldiers who had never seen their faces, I discovered that can be surrounded by thousands
of others, and still feel entirely alone.
The crossings had brought together three versions of the same child.
We had been shaped by different worlds, but somehow found each other.
And now the war had separated us, as easily.
as it had brought us together.
When I saw Keshe and Rook again,
I almost didn't recognize how much they had changed.
We had grown older in the space of a war.
For a moment,
all three of us stood together as we had.
In Ashbridge, and I wanted to believe that was enough.
Fred's armies were everywhere.
Their movements were precise, almost beautiful in their order.
There was no anger in them that I could see.
They advanced, because the mind directed and believed, and found the only acceptable future.
When the fighting reached us, threat could have allowed us to die.
We were opposing everything it had built.
Instead, its creatures turned away from their advance
and placed themselves between us
and the destruction.
For a brief moment,
A whole movement seemed uncertain.
Threaded tried to free itself from attachment, from grief, from everything it considered
weakness.
Yet it could not bear to lose the three children, who at once carried it in a wooden box.
I understood, then, that threat had never become free of emotion, and it simply decided that
its own feelings were different from everyone else's.
It wanted to save the world from itself, and it could not see how much of itself.
It had brought into that world, the war against threat ended, although endings rarely looked
the way we imagined them.
The great network fell, silent armies stopped moving, in place where there had been all
a fight, a kick.
People began looking for one another.
For years,
the world had been divided by their histories,
their laws,
and their fears.
In the end,
they had needed one another to fight.
I wish I could say that made them lies.
Perhaps it only made them more careful.
Sometimes I think about the creature we found at Ashbridge.
I remember I followed my finger across the glass.
I remember how proud I felt when it understood me.
I have never been certain, when understanding the games or something else.
I still have the drawings I made to point a page.
The bridge.
The road three friends sitting beside the fire.
I have things in those pages that I can remember more clearly.
and the victories, and the feats people write about in their history.
I have wondered whether or not I'm wrong to break that cliff.
I will never remember how small a friend friends are.
I know, I know, I would have done it again.
I only wish we'd understood that saving a life and teaching it to us late to the light will not fade away.
I can still hear the glass breaking.
